items.text: Obey your master with fear, not only if he is good and gentle, but also if he is harsh.
items.citation: Book of Homilies, An Exhortation concerning Good Order and Obedience to Rulers and Magistrates
items.quote: Seruauntes obeye your Masters with feare, not onely, if they be good and gentle, but also, if they bee frowarde.

work: Book of Homilies: 'An Exhortacion concernyng good ordre and obedience' and 'An H
heading: An Homilee of the state of Matrimonie (Second Tome of Homilees, 1571)

items.text: Live together in lawful, perpetual, and faithful friendship as God has ordained.
items.citation: Book of Homilies, An Homilee of the state of Matrimonie (Second Tome of Homilees, 1571)
items.quote: man & woman should liue lawfully in a perpetuall frendly felowship

items.text: Keep yourself chaste and faithful within marriage, shunning all fornication and uncleanness.
items.citation: Book of Homilies, An Homilee of the state of Matrimonie (Second Tome of Homilees, 1571)
items.quote: God hath straitly forbidden all whoredome and vncleannesse

items.text: Bring up your children in the knowledge of God's word and true religion.
items.citation: Book of Homilies, An Homilee of the state of Matrimonie (Second Tome of Homilees, 1571)
items.quote: they be brought vp by ye parents godly, in the knowledge of Gods word

items.text: Resist the devil's attempts to break or embitter the marriage bond; give him no entry.
items.citation: Book of Homilies, An Homilee of the state of Matrimonie (Second Tome of Homilees, 1571)
items.quote: the deuill will assaye to attempt all thinges to interrupte and hynder your heartes and godly purpose, if ye will geue him anye entrye

work: Book of Homilies: 'An Exhortacion concernyng good ordre and obedience' and 'An H
heading: An Exhortacion, concernyng good ordre and obedience, to rulers and magistrates (First Book of Homilies, 1547)

items.text: Do not rebel against your father; Absalom's rebellion against his father King David was punished with a strange and notable death.
items.citation: Book of Homilies, An Exhortacion concernyng good ordre and obedience, to rulers and magistrates
items.quote: Absalon also, rebelling against his father king Dauid, was punished with a straunge and notable death.

items.text: Do not obey your father if he commands anything contrary to God's commandments; obey God rather than man.
items.citation: Book of Homilies, An Exhortacion concernyng good ordre and obedience, to rulers and magistrates
items.quote: we may not obey Kynges, Magistrates, or any other, (though thei be our awne fathers) if thei would cōmaunde vs to do any thyng, contrary to Gods cōmaundemētes.

items.text: Even when you must not obey your father's unlawful command, do not violently resist or rebel against him; patiently suffer wrongs and leave judgment to God.
items.citation: Book of Homilies, An Exhortacion concernyng good ordre and obedience, to rulers and magistrates
items.quote: we maye not in any wyse resist violētly, or rebell against rulers

work: Book of Homilies: 'An Exhortacion concernyng good ordre and obedience' and 'An H
heading: An Homilee of the state of Matrimonie (Second Tome of Homilees, 1571)

items.text: Honor your wife as the weaker vessel and joint heir of the grace of life, dealing with her according to knowledge, so that your prayers are not hindered.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: You husbandes deale with your wyues accordyng to knowledge, geuing honour to the wyfe, as vnto the weaker vessell, & as vnto them that are heyres also of the grace of lyfe, that your prayers be not hyndered.

items.text: Use moderation and not tyranny as head of your wife; yield to her in some things, and forbear her frailties.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: he ought to be the leader & aucthour of loue, in cherishing and increasing concorde, whiche then shall take place, if he will vse measurablenesse and not tirannie, & if he yelde some thinges to the woman.

items.text: Never beat or strike your wife; to lay violent hands on her is a great shame and unworthy of a Christian man.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: Let there be none so greeuous fault to compell you to beate your wyues... it is a great shame for a man to beate his bonde seruaunt, muche more rebuke it is, to lay vyolent handes vppon his free woman.

items.text: Do not cast out or divorce your wife for any fault; bear with her patiently and expect reward from God.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: that lawe which forbiddeth that a man shoulde caste out his wyfe what faulte soeuer she be combred with, thou shalt haue a very great rewarde
items.conflict: Conflicts with Matthew 5:32 and 19:9 which permit divorce for adultery.

items.text: Be in subjection to your husband and obey him; do not command or control him, but apply yourself to his will.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: Ye wyues, be ye in subiection to obey your owne husband. To obey, is another thyng then to comptrole or commaund.

items.text: Obey your husband as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord, and set your hope in God.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling hym lord, whose daughters ye be (saith he) if ye folowe her example.

items.text: Do not speak against or upbraid your husband for his decisions; keep silence as Sara did when Abraham risked his life for Lot.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: But Sara neither said nor thought such words, but she kept her self in scilence in al thynges.

items.text: When you have offended your husband, acknowledge your fault, ask forgiveness, and promise to amend.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: let them acknowledge their follies, and say: My husband, so it is, that by my anger I was compelled to do this or that, forgeue it me, and hereafter I wyll take better heed.

items.text: Pray for each other and together, continually asking God to preserve concord and resist the devil's attempts to divide you.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: maryed persons must apply their myndes in moste earnest wyse to concorde, and must craue continually of God the helpe of his holy spirite, so to rule their heartes, and to knit their myndes together, that they be not disseuered by any diuision of discorde.

items.text: Do your own duty in marriage rather than demanding the other's duty; perform what belongs to yourself.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: let eyther partie be redy & willyng to perfourme that which belongeth specially to them selfe.

items.text: Do not taunt or despise your wife if she is poor or simple; be courteous, for she is your body and one flesh with you.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: if she be poore, vpbrayde her not, if she be simple, taunt her not, but be the more curteous. For she is thy body, and made one fleshe with thee.

items.text: If your wife is wrathful or has faults, admonish her with good counsel, pray for her, and help her overcome her affections, rather than chafing or beating her.
items.citation: Homily of the State of Matrimony
items.quote: if she be a wrathfull woman, a drunkarde, and beastly... For this cause bewayle her the more. Chafe not in anger, but pray to almyghtie God. Let her be admonished and holpen with good counsayle.
